name: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
title: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
answer: Virtual surgical rehearsal is the practice of building a patient specific model of the anatomy and the planned operation, then running the procedure in simulation before anyone enters the operating room. It sits inside surgical robotics and navigation, where the same imaging, registration and instrument tracking used in the live case are reused offline. The scope covers bony and soft tissue procedures, from craniofacial reconstruction to tumour resection, and increasingly covers the rehearsal of robot assisted steps rather than only the approach. It is distinct from generic surgical training, because the model is the individual patient rather than a teaching case.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Virtual surgical rehearsal is the practice of building a patient specific model of the anatomy and the planned operation, then running the procedure in simulation before anyone enters the operating room. It sits inside surgical robotics and navigation, where the same imaging, registration and instrument tracking used in the live case are reused offline. The scope covers bony and soft tissue procedures, from craniofacial reconstruction to tumour resection, and increasingly covers the rehearsal of robot assisted steps rather than only the approach. It is distinct from generic surgical training, because the model is the individual patient rather than a teaching case.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The pipeline starts with imaging, most often CT or MRI, sometimes ultrasound or endoscopic video, and turns it into a segmented three dimensional model of the target and the structures to avoid. That model runs on a workstation or a headset, with haptic devices for force feedback and a tracking system that mirrors the navigation hardware used in theatre. Segmentation and registration are the heavy steps, and they are where machine learning has entered, since manual contouring of a tumour or a nerve is slow and operator dependent. The rehearsal environment is usually separate from the certified intraoperative system, so the model has to be transferred and re registered before it can guide anything.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work begins with image acquisition and segmentation, then a planning step where the surgeon chooses an approach, defines resection margins and positions implants or instruments. The rehearsal itself is a simulation, either a physics based model of tissue deformation or a kinematic model of the robot arm, and the surgeon steps through the sequence and adjusts the plan. Fidelity is the central problem, because soft tissue moves and bleeds in ways a model approximates, so rehearsal is used to test decisions rather than to predict exact geometry. Validation is usually retrospective, comparing the rehearsed plan against what was actually found and done, and prospective trials are fewer.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The patient images and the derived model are identifiable health data, so consent, storage and cross border transfer all apply, and a model that is reused for other patients raises questions the original consent may not cover. If the rehearsal output is used to guide a real operation, the software may fall under medical device regulation, and the line between a planning aid and a navigation device matters for clearance. Liability is shared across the surgeon, the hospital and the software vendor, and this site tracks 6 active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, which shows how that allocation is being tested. Provenance of the model, meaning which scan, which segmentation version and which plan, needs to be recorded so the rehearsal can be audited after the case.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward rehearsal that is fast enough to sit inside the clinical workflow, generated from the same scan that is already being taken, rather than a separate research exercise. Better soft tissue simulation and patient specific material properties are the main technical gaps, alongside registration that survives movement and deformation in the live case. As robot platforms open their kinematics to third party planning software, rehearsal and intraoperative navigation are likely to merge into one environment. The regulatory question of when a rehearsal becomes a device that guides care will shape adoption more than the simulation quality itself.
